title: READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent's Meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy Koo Yoon-cheol of the Republic of Korea
summary: Secretary Bessent met with South Korea's Deputy Prime Minister Koo to discuss the U.S.-Korea Trade and Investment Agreement and its implementation, along with a finalized critical minerals framework. The two sides agreed that excessive volatility in the Korean won is not desirable and will continue FX market consultations.
key_points: U.S.-Korea Trade and Investment Agreement discussed with focus on swift implementation
Critical minerals framework between U.S. and South Korea finalized, aimed at deepening collaboration and addressing non-market practices
Both sides expressed support for South Korea as a global AI hub and AI's role in G20 productivity goals
Secretary Bessent and Minister Koo agreed excessive Korean won volatility is undesirable and will continue FX market consultations
No specific numbers, dates, or concrete policy actions announced
why_it_matters: This readout reflects ongoing U.S.-Korea diplomatic engagement on trade and FX issues. The explicit mention that both sides view Korean won volatility as undesirable signals potential coordinated concern about currency moves, though no specific policy commitments were made. The critical minerals framework has implications for supply chain diversification in strategic sectors.

The FX consultation language suggests both governments are monitoring won volatility, though no specific intervention threshold or policy response was stated.
